representativeRepos.readmeText:
T3 Code

 The open-source control plane for coding agents.

 Download ·
 iOS ·
 Android ·
 Web ·
 Docs ·
 Discord

 T3 Code runs the coding agents on your machine and gives them one fast interface. Start a thread at your desk, then approve the next step from your phone.

 It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok Build, Antigravity, Kiro, Pi, Muse Code, fx, and any ACP agent. If an agent is set up on your computer, T3 Code can control it.

 What you get

- Your subscriptions. T3 Code does not resell tokens. It drives the agents you are already signed in to.

- Every agent in one place. Change models in the middle of a thread. Let Claude hand a task to Codex.

- Desktop, web, and phone. One server, and every client shows the same threads. There are apps for iOS and Android.

- Remote ready. Run agents on any machine. Connect over your local network, Tailscale, or T3 Connect .

- Git built in. Each thread can work in its own worktree. Review the diff, then commit, push, and open a pull request with one button.

- Fast. Performance is a feature here. We measure it, and we treat a dropped frame as a bug.

- Open. MIT licensed. If you don't like something, fork it.

 Install

 Desktop app

 Download T3 Code for macOS, Windows, or Linux. You can also use a package manager:

 Platform
 Command

 macOS
 brew install --cask t3-code

 Windows
 winget install T3Tools.T3Code or scoop install extras/t3code

 Arch Linux
 yay -S t3code-bin

 Nix
 nix profile add github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable#t3code

 Debian, Ubuntu
 .deb from Releases

 Command line

 This installs the t3 command. Run t3 to start the server and open the web app.

 curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh

 On Windows, in PowerShell:

 irm https: // t3.codes / install.ps1 | iex

 To try it once without an install, run npx t3@latest .

 Phone

 Get the app from the App Store or Google Play . Then follow remote access to connect it to your computer.

 Sign in to an agent

 T3 Code needs one agent that is installed and signed in. For example, install Claude Code and run claude auth login , or install Codex CLI and run codex login .

 Provider setup has the steps for each agent. Install T3 Code covers nightly builds, AppImage, WSL, and NixOS.

 "Wait, what are you selling me?"

 Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents. We were inspired by existing solutions like the Codex desktop app, Conductor, Claude Desktop and Cursor Glass, but none met our bar.

 We wanted something performant, remote-ready, and truly open. If we ever go the wrong direction, we want you to have everything you need to fork and build the tool that you want.

 Documentation

- Install and first run

- Remote access from a phone or another machine

- Permission modes

- Source control

- Connect outside agents over MCP

- FAQ

 All docs has the full list.

 Contributing

 We have limited review capacity. Small, focused fixes are the most likely to be merged. Features need an approved discussion first.

- Read CONTRIBUTING.md before you report a bug or open a pull request.

- Put feature requests in Ideas .

- Build from source with the development runbook . The architecture overview explains how it works.

- Get help in Discord .

representativeRepos.readmeText:
Impeccable

 The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with polish and bolder , review with critique and audit , and catch AI slop before it ships.

 From your project root:

 npx impeccable install

 Reload your coding tool, then run /impeccable init in your agent ( $impeccable init on Codex).

 Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Replit Agent, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and Veto. Full docs live at impeccable.style/docs .

 Without Impeccable
 With Impeccable

 Same model (Fable 5.1), same brief: a fourteen-room family guesthouse on the Ligurian coast. Without Impeccable, it builds the tasteful default: cream page, thin serif, italic accent, pill buttons. With it, the page is built around one picture: the house at night, seen from the water.

 For a full project, see the Neo Mirai case study : a conference site taken from mockup to shipped page.

 Why

 Inter for everything. Purple-to-blue gradients. Cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, a rounded-square icon tile above every heading. Ask an agent for a page with no other guidance and these show up again and again, across models and projects.

- Words for what you want. "Make it pop" leaves your agent to guess. /impeccable bolder the pricing cards loads a playbook written for that one move and points it at one target.

- A reviewer. critique scores the design against usability heuristics and ranks what to fix first. audit checks accessibility, performance, theming, and responsive behavior, with findings ranked P0 (blocking) to P3 (polish).

- A slop detector. 62 deterministic rules flag the tells above, plus quality problems like cramped padding and skipped headings. No LLM, no API key.

 Impeccable is strongest on interfaces that already exist: point it at a page or a component and iterate. It builds new pages too; see Build something new for how to get the most out of that harder mode. To start, pick one component:

 /impeccable critique the pricing cards

 How it works

 Run /impeccable init once per project. It reads your code, asks only what it can't infer (who the product is for, what it needs to do, the constraints), and writes PRODUCT.md . Every later command reads it. Run /impeccable document to capture your existing visual system in DESIGN.md , so changes stay on-brand. More on context files .

 Then name a command and a target:

 /impeccable critique the onboarding flow
/impeccable quieter the landing page
/impeccable polish settings
/impeccable harden checkout

 Or just describe what you want: /impeccable redo this hero section . Narrow targets get better results; a single section reviewed closely beats a whole page at a glance. Pin a command you use often with /impeccable pin audit to get /audit as its own shortcut.

 24 commands

 Commands

 Steer
 bolder amplifies safe designs · quieter tones down loud ones · distill removes what the page doesn't need · colorize brings color to a gray interface · typeset fixes fonts, hierarchy, and sizing · layout fixes spacing and rhythm · animate adds transitions and interaction feedback · delight adds personality · overdrive goes for shaders, spring physics, and scroll-driven effects

 Review
 critique is a scored UX review · audit is a technical quality report

 Finish
 polish is the final pass before shipping · harden covers errors, i18n, overflow, and edge cases · clarify rewrites unclear copy · adapt handles screen sizes and devices · optimize fixes loading and rendering performance · onboard designs first-run flows and empty states

 Iterate live
 live lets you pick an element in the browser and cycle through variants · generate produces variants of a named element without manual picking

 Plan and set up
 shape plans UX before code · init writes PRODUCT.md · document writes DESIGN.md · extract pulls repeated patterns into your design system

 The 24th, craft , is a deprecated alias for a plain build request. Type /impeccable alone to see the list in your agent. Each command has its own page: impeccable.style/docs .

 On Codex, open /skills or type $impeccable instead of the slash command.

 Live mode

 /impeccable live opens your running dev server with an overlay. Select an element, pick a direction, and Impeccable hot-swaps variants in place. Accept one and it is written back to your source. It works with Vite, Next, SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt, and plain HTML. Iterate in the browser .

 Live mode edits a local checkout only; don't inject it into a deployed site or weaken a production CSP to make it work. Applying copy edits runs your package.json 's optional impeccable:manual-edit-validate script with your permissions, so review it before using live mode in an unfamiliar repo.

 Apply sends staged copy edits to your chat agent while a live session is polling. If none has polled in the last minute, it runs the codex CLI from your PATH instead (or claude when codex is missing), with approvals, permission checks, and sandboxing off ( --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox or --permission-mode bypassPermissions ) and your environment inherited. Its prompt carries the staged edits, the edited elements' HTML and nearby text, the page URL, and candidate source paths. Set IMPECCABLE_LIVE_COPY_AGENT=chat in the environment that starts live mode to keep Apply in your chat session, or off to disable Apply. The server reads it once at startup.

 Three ways to run the detector

 In your agent. The design hook scans every UI file your agent edits and hands the findings back before the agent calls the work done. This is where most slop gets caught: without the hook, the detector only runs when someone remembers to run it. It's available on Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, and Hermes Agent, and the installer sets it up. Say yes. Automatic design checks .

 In CI or your terminal. The CLI needs no agent:

 npx impeccable detect src/ # scan a directory
npx impeccable detect https://example.com # scan a rendered page (uses your installed Chrome or Edge)
npx impeccable detect --json . # machine-readable output
npx impeccable detect --github src/ # GitHub Actions annotations
npx impeccable detect --list-rules # every rule with its id and description

 Source files like JSX and TSX get the pattern rules only. Rules that need a rendered page, such as low contrast and tiny text, run when you scan a URL, so point the CLI at your dev server too: npx impeccable detect http://localhost:5173 .

 Exit code 2 means findings, 1 means a target couldn't be scanned. To allow your brand font everywhere, run npx impeccable ignores add-value overused-font Inter --reason "Brand font" . To turn a rule off for one file, add a comment: <!-- impeccable-disable overused-font: exported brand doc --> . Run a detector scan · Configuration and ignores .

 In your browser. The Chrome extension overlays the same findings on any live page, yours or anyone else's. Review with a visual overlay .

 Installation

 npx impeccable install

 The installer detects your coding tools, asks whether to install for this project or globally, and offers the design hook where your tool supports one. Accept the hook. Reload your tool afterward. npx impeccable update refreshes an existing install. For scripts, pass --providers=claude,codex,cursor and --scope=project|global .

 Three tools need one more step before the hook runs. In Codex, open /hooks and approve the project hook (again after an update that changes it). In Grok Build, run /hooks-trust or launch with --trust . In Hermes Agent, the hook is a plugin: run hermes plugins enable impeccable-design-hook once. Allow the hook in your harness .

 Node is only needed for npx . The skill itself runs a self-contained engine binary that ships next to it or downloads once into ~/.impeccable/bin/ .

 Claude Code, Copilot, and Grok plugins
 Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable , then open /plugin and install Impeccable.

 GitHub Copilot in VS Code: install Impeccable from the Visual Studio Marketplace or run code --install-extension renaissance-geek.impeccable . Needs VS Code 1.109.3+, Copilot Chat, and a trusted workspace. It installs the skill without the hook. Details .

 Grok Build: grok plugin install pbakaus/impeccable#plugin --trust installs the skill, agents, and hook.

 Git submodule (a pinned version for the whole team)
 git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable vendor/impeccable
npx impeccable link --source=vendor/impeccable --providers=claude,cursor

 Commit .gitmodules , the submodule, and the generated links. Teammates run git submodule update --init --recursive . To upgrade, run git submodule update --remote vendor/impeccable , rerun the link command, and commit. Linking installs skills, not hooks. Existing skill folders stay put unless you pass --force .

 Manual copy, no Node required
 Download the ZIP for your tool from impeccable.style , or clone this repo: each tool's build is committed at the repo root. Copy skills/impeccable from the folder below into the same place in your project, or into the global folder.

 Tool
 Repo folder
 Global skills folder

 Claude Code
 .claude/
 ~/.claude/skills/

 Cursor
 .cursor/

 Codex CLI, Replit Agent
 .agents/
 ~/.agents/skills/

 Devin
 .devin/
 ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/devin/skills/

 GitHub Copilot
 .github/

 Gemini CLI
 .gemini/

 Google Antigravity
 .agent/
 ~/.gemini/config/skills/

 OpenCode
 .opencode/

 Grok Build
 .grok/
 ~/.grok/skills/

 Hermes Agent
 .hermes/
 ${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/

 DeepSeek Harness
 .dsh/
 ${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/

 Pi
 .pi/

 Qoder
 .qoder/
 ~/.qoder/skills/

 Rovo Dev
 .rovodev/
 ~/.rovodev/skills/

 Mistral Vibe
 .vibe/
 ~/.vibe/skills/

 Trae
 .trae/
 ~/.trae/skills/

 Trae China
 .trae-cn/
 ~/.trae-cn/skills/

 For example: mkdir -p your-project/.claude/skills && cp -r .claude/skills/impeccable your-project/.claude/skills/ .

 Notes:

- A manual copy skips the design hook and subagents. Run npx impeccable install to get them; it writes each tool's hook pointing at the right skill path.

- OpenCode also needs .opencode/commands/impeccable.md copied into your project's .opencode/commands/ to provide /impeccable .

- Hermes asks you to trust project-local skills once: run hermes skills trust from the project root. Global installs need no trust step.

- Cursor and Gemini CLI may need Agent Skills enabled in settings. See the Cursor and Gemini CLI skills docs.

- Restart Trae after copying.

- impeccable install and update manage a DeepSeek Harness global copy only when DSH_HOME is inside your home directory.

 Project files and git

 Impeccable writes its working files under .impeccable/ . A few are shared project artifacts and belong in the repo: config.json , live/config.json , design.json , surfaces/*.md , and critique/*.md . Keep PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md in the repo too. The rest is screenshots, caches, and runtime state.

 Copy the .gitignore entries
 # impeccable-ignore-start
 # Ephemeral output, runtime state, and per-dev overrides.
 # The **/ prefix covers .impeccable at the repo root or in a nested workspace.
 # Shared artifacts stay tracked: config.json, live/config.json,
 # design.json, surfaces/*.md, critique/*.md.
 ** / .impeccable / config.local.json
 ** / .impeccable / hook.cache.json
 ** / .impeccable / hook.pending.json
 ** / .impeccable / * .png
 ** / .impeccable / review /
 ** / .impeccable / questions /
 ** / .impeccable / live / server.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / sessions /
 ** / .impeccable / live / previews /
 ** / .impeccable / live / annotations /
 ** / .impeccable / live / cache /
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-apply-transaction.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-events.jsonl
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-evidence /
 ** / .impeccable / live / pending-manual-edits.json
 ** / .impeccab...

readmeText:
Knowledge Work Plugins

 Plugins that turn Claude into a specialist for your role, team, and company. Built for Claude Cowork , also compatible with Claude Code .

 Why Plugins

 Cowork lets you set the goal and Claude delivers finished, professional work. Plugins let you go further: tell Claude how you like work done, which tools and data to pull from, how to handle critical workflows, and what slash commands to expose — so your team gets better and more consistent outcomes.

 Each plugin bundles the skills, connectors, slash commands, and sub-agents for a specific job function. Out of the box, they give Claude a strong starting point for helping anyone in that role. The real power comes when you customize them for your company — your tools, your terminology, your processes — so Claude works like it was built for your team.

 Plugin Marketplace

 We're open-sourcing 11 plugins built and inspired by our own work:

 Plugin
 How it helps
 Connectors

 productivity
 Manage tasks, calendars, daily workflows, and personal context so you spend less time repeating yourself.
 Slack, Notion, Asana, Linear, Jira, Monday, ClickUp, Microsoft 365

 sales
 Research prospects, prep for calls, review your pipeline, draft outreach, and build competitive battlecards.
 Slack, HubSpot, Close, Clay, ZoomInfo, Notion, Jira, Fireflies, Microsoft 365

 customer-support
 Triage tickets, draft responses, package escalations, research customer context, and turn resolved issues into knowledge base articles.
 Slack, Intercom, HubSpot, Guru, Jira, Notion, Microsoft 365

 product-management
 Write specs, plan roadmaps, synthesize user research, keep stakeholders updated, and track the competitive landscape.
 Slack, Linear, Asana, Monday, ClickUp, Jira, Notion, Figma, Amplitude, Pendo, Intercom, Fireflies

 marketing
 Draft content, plan campaigns, enforce brand voice, brief on competitors, and report on performance across channels.
 Slack, Canva, Figma, HubSpot, Amplitude, Notion, Ahrefs, SimilarWeb, Klaviyo

 legal
 Review contracts, triage NDAs, navigate compliance, assess risk, prep for meetings, and draft templated responses.
 Slack, Box, Egnyte, Jira, Microsoft 365

 finance
 Prep journal entries, reconcile accounts, generate financial statements, analyze variances, manage close, and support audits.
 Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, Slack, Microsoft 365

 data
 Query, visualize, and interpret datasets — write SQL, run statistical analysis, build dashboards, and validate your work before sharing.
 Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, Definite, Hex, Amplitude, Jira

 enterprise-search
 Find anything across email, chat, docs, and wikis — one query across all your company's tools.
 Slack, Notion, Guru, Jira, Asana, Microsoft 365

 bio-research
 Connect to preclinical research tools and databases (literature search, genomics analysis, target prioritization) to accelerate early-stage life sciences R&D.
 PubMed, BioRender, bioRxiv, ClinicalTrials.gov, ChEMBL, Synapse, Wiley, Owkin, Open Targets, Benchling

 cowork-plugin-management
 Create new plugins or customize existing ones for your organization's specific tools and workflows.
 —

 Install these directly from Cowork, browse the full collection here on GitHub, or build your own.

 Getting Started

 Cowork

 Install plugins from claude.com/plugins .

 Claude Code

 # Add the marketplace first
claude plugin marketplace add anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins

 # Then install a specific plugin
claude plugin install sales@knowledge-work-plugins

 Once installed, plugins activate automatically. Skills fire when relevant, and slash commands are available in your session (e.g., /sales:call-prep , /data:write-query ).

 How Plugins Work

 Every plugin follows the same structure:

 plugin-name/
├── .claude-plugin/plugin.json # Manifest
├── .mcp.json # Tool connections
├── commands/ # Slash commands you invoke explicitly
└── skills/ # Domain knowledge Claude draws on automatically

- Skills encode the domain expertise, best practices, and step-by-step workflows Claude needs to give you useful help. Claude draws on them automatically when relevant.

- Commands are explicit actions you trigger (e.g., /finance:reconciliation , /product-management:write-spec ).

- Connectors wire Claude to the external tools your role depends on — CRMs, project trackers, data warehouses, design tools, and more — via MCP servers .

 Every component is file-based — markdown and JSON, no code, no infrastructure, no build steps.

 Making Them Yours

 These plugins are generic starting points. They become much more useful when you customize them for how your company actually works:

- Swap connectors — Edit .mcp.json to point at your specific tool stack.

- Add company context — Drop your terminology, org structure, and processes into skill files so Claude understands your world.

- Adjust workflows — Modify skill instructions to match how your team actually does things, not how a textbook says to.

- Build new plugins — Use the cowork-plugin-management plugin or follow the structure above to create plugins for roles and workflows we haven't covered yet.

 As your team builds and shares plugins, Claude becomes a cross-functional expert. The context you define gets baked into every relevant interaction, so leaders and admins can spend less time enforcing processes and more time improving them.

 Contributing

 Plugins are just markdown files. Fork the repo, make your changes, and submit a PR.

representativeRepos.readmeText:
security-audit

 A coding-agent skill that turns your agent into a security auditor. It orchestrates isolated agents through reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured output, independent record verification, and target-neutral reporting.

 This is the skill that seeded Cloudflare's vulnerability discovery harness, described in Build your own vulnerability harness . The harness grew into a multi-stage, fleet-wide system; this skill is the single-repo starting point it evolved from.

 What it does

 The skill runs a structured audit in six phases:

- Reconnaissance -- map architecture, trust boundaries, input surfaces, prior evidence, and deterministic coverage in architecture.md and coverage-ledger.json .

- Coverage-led hunting -- assign isolated hunters from ledger units, record their checks, and use coverage critics to find gaps.

- Candidate validation -- give every unique candidate to a fresh verifier that tries to disprove it.

- Structured output -- write confirmed , needs_validation , and rejected records to findings.json and validate them against report-schema.json .

- Independent record verification -- fresh agents verify final source claims. Material replacements receive another independent verifier.

- Target-neutral reporting -- derive REPORT.md , FINDINGS-DETAIL.md , and NEEDS-VALIDATION.md from the verified records and coverage ledger.

 The parent runs validate-coverage-ledger.cjs after creating the ledger and after each later ledger update. It runs validate-findings.cjs in Phase 4 and again after every Phase 5 replacement.

 The verdicts are distinct: confirmed has a complete source trace and bounded observed result, needs_validation has an exact unresolved fact and no severity, and rejected records a disproved candidate.

 Multiple runs against the same repo are additive. The skill uses prior ledgers and findings to target gaps, revalidate changed source, and carry forward current-source evidence without treating stale or unresolved work as covered.

 Files

 File
 Purpose

 SKILL.md
 Setup, core principles, platform terminology, workflow overview, and audit anti-patterns

 RECONNAISSANCE.md
 Phase 1 reconnaissance prompts and synthesis instructions

 HUNTING.md
 Phase 2 orchestration, hunting methodology, and validation rules

 ATTACK-CLASSES.md
 Core, wildcard, and obvious-things attack prompts

 MEMORY-SAFETY-AND-BINARY.md
 Memory-safety, binary, and kernel hunting classes for native targets

 AI-AND-LLM.md
 Prompt-injection, agent/tool, and output-handling hunting classes for LLM-backed targets

 WEB-PROTOCOL-AND-AUTH.md
 HTTP request-framing, cache, and authentication-protocol hunting classes for HTTP-protocol and auth targets

 CLIENT-SIDE.md
 DOM-injection, messaging-trust, UI-redress, and prototype-pollution hunting classes for client-side/browser targets

 SUPPLY-CHAIN-AND-RELEASE.md
 Dependency, CI, release, signing, update, plugin, and extension hunting classes

 CLOUD-AND-DEPLOYMENT.md
 IAM, infrastructure-as-code, container, serverless, ingress, and runtime-configuration hunting classes

 PROTOCOLS-RPC-AND-MESSAGING.md
 RPC, serialization, queue, broker, webhook, and streaming-protocol hunting classes

 RESOURCE-EXHAUSTION-AND-AVAILABILITY.md
 Shared resource, quota, queue, worker, and operator-spend hunting classes

 DATA-ISOLATION-AND-LIFECYCLE.md
 Tenant isolation, cache, search, export, backup, migration, deletion, and restore hunting classes

 DESKTOP-MOBILE-AND-LOCAL-IPC.md
 Native app, deep-link, webview, exported-component, helper, daemon, and local-IPC hunting classes

 VALIDATION-AND-REPORTING.md
 Phases 3–6 candidate validation, structured output, record verification, and reporting

 report-schema.json
 JSON schema for all three findings.json verdicts

 validate-findings.cjs
 Zero-dependency validator for findings.json in Phases 4 and 5

 validate-findings.test.cjs
 Findings-validator tests and producer-compatible fixture checks

 validate-coverage-ledger.cjs
 Zero-dependency validator for coverage-ledger.json in Phases 1–5

 validate-coverage-ledger.test.cjs
 Coverage-ledger validator tests

 Installation

 Install the skill with the Skills CLI :

 npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill \
 --skill security-audit

 Use --global for a user-level installation:

 npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill \
 --skill security-audit \
 --global

 Run npx skills --help for agent-selection and non-interactive options.

 Usage

 Start your coding agent in (or pointed at) the codebase you want to audit, then ask it to do a security audit:

 security audit this codebase

 find security vulnerabilities in ./src

 do a security review, output to ~/audits/my-project

 The skill activates automatically when the request matches its trigger (security audit, find vulnerabilities, pen-test the code, etc.). A direct codebase audit or pen-test request uses full audit mode. Security questions and focused vulnerability work use guidance mode unless you request report artifacts. In full audit mode, an unspecified output directory defaults to ~/security-audit-skill/<repo-name>/run-<N> . The workflow writes inside the target repository only when you explicitly select a directory that version control ignores.

 Requirements

- A coding agent with a model that supports tool use and parallel sub-agents

- Node.js for the zero-dependency findings and coverage-ledger validators

- An OS-enforced sandbox for target-controlled builds, tests, processes, browsers, emulators, fuzzers, and fixtures. It must disable external networking, use a sanitized allowlisted environment, enforce resource limits, and allow writes only to assigned scratch paths. Without these controls, the workflow keeps the lead as needs_validation instead of executing target code.

 Design principles

- Only confirm established boundary failures. Keep a source-grounded blocked lead as needs_validation with its exact unresolved fact.

- Adversarial validation. The agent that checks a finding is never the agent that found it.

- Severity requires impact. Likelihood x impact, not deviation from a checklist.

- Defense-in-depth gaps are not vulnerabilities. If Layer A prevents the attack, the absence of Layer B is a hardening note.

- Multiple runs improve coverage. In our test runs, a single run found roughly half of the vulnerabilities that repeated runs found in total.

 Contact

 Questions, feedback, or comparing notes on AI-driven security tooling: security-ai-research@cloudflare.com

 License

 MIT -- see LICENSE .

representativeRepos.readmeText:
T3 Code

 The open-source control plane for coding agents.

 Download ·
 iOS ·
 Android ·
 Web ·
 Docs ·
 Discord

 T3 Code runs the coding agents on your machine and gives them one fast interface. Start a thread at your desk, then approve the next step from your phone.

 It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok Build, Antigravity, Kiro, Pi, Muse Code, fx, and any ACP agent. If an agent is set up on your computer, T3 Code can control it.

 What you get

- Your subscriptions. T3 Code does not resell tokens. It drives the agents you are already signed in to.

- Every agent in one place. Change models in the middle of a thread. Let Claude hand a task to Codex.

- Desktop, web, and phone. One server, and every client shows the same threads. There are apps for iOS and Android.

- Remote ready. Run agents on any machine. Connect over your local network, Tailscale, or T3 Connect .

- Git built in. Each thread can work in its own worktree. Review the diff, then commit, push, and open a pull request with one button.

- Fast. Performance is a feature here. We measure it, and we treat a dropped frame as a bug.

- Open. MIT licensed. If you don't like something, fork it.

 Install

 Desktop app

 Download T3 Code for macOS, Windows, or Linux. You can also use a package manager:

 Platform
 Command

 macOS
 brew install --cask t3-code

 Windows
 winget install T3Tools.T3Code or scoop install extras/t3code

 Arch Linux
 yay -S t3code-bin

 Nix
 nix profile add github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable#t3code

 Debian, Ubuntu
 .deb from Releases

 Command line

 This installs the t3 command. Run t3 to start the server and open the web app.

 curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh

 On Windows, in PowerShell:

 irm https: // t3.codes / install.ps1 | iex

 To try it once without an install, run npx t3@latest .

 Phone

 Get the app from the App Store or Google Play . Then follow remote access to connect it to your computer.

 Sign in to an agent

 T3 Code needs one agent that is installed and signed in. For example, install Claude Code and run claude auth login , or install Codex CLI and run codex login .

 Provider setup has the steps for each agent. Install T3 Code covers nightly builds, AppImage, WSL, and NixOS.

 Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents. We were inspired by existing solutions like the Codex desktop app, Conductor, Claude Desktop and Cursor Glass, but none met our bar.

 We wanted something performant, remote-ready, and truly open. If we ever go the wrong direction, we want you to have everything you need to fork and build the tool that you want.

 Documentation

- Install and first run

- Remote access from a phone or another machine

- Permission modes

- Source control

- Connect outside agents over MCP

- FAQ

 All docs has the full list.

 Contributing

 We have limited review capacity. Small, focused fixes are the most likely to be merged. Features need an approved discussion first.

- Read CONTRIBUTING.md before you report a bug or open a pull request.

- Put feature requests in Ideas .

- Build from source with the development runbook . The architecture overview explains how it works.

- Get help in Discord .

representativeRepos.readmeText:
Impeccable

 The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with polish and bolder , review with critique and audit , and catch AI slop before it ships.

 From your project root:

 npx impeccable install

 Reload your coding tool, then run /impeccable init in your agent ( $impeccable init on Codex).

 Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Replit Agent, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and Veto. Full docs live at impeccable.style/docs .

 Without Impeccable
 With Impeccable

 Same model (Fable 5.1), same brief: a fourteen-room family guesthouse on the Ligurian coast. Without Impeccable, it builds the tasteful default: cream page, thin serif, italic accent, pill buttons. With it, the page is built around one picture: the house at night, seen from the water.

 For a full project, see the Neo Mirai case study : a conference site taken from mockup to shipped page.

 Why

 Inter for everything. Purple-to-blue gradients. Cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, a rounded-square icon tile above every heading. Ask an agent for a page with no other guidance and these show up again and again, across models and projects.

- Words for what you want. "Make it pop" leaves your agent to guess. /impeccable bolder the pricing cards loads a playbook written for that one move and points it at one target.

- A reviewer. critique scores the design against usability heuristics and ranks what to fix first. audit checks accessibility, performance, theming, and responsive behavior, with findings ranked P0 (blocking) to P3 (polish).

- A slop detector. 62 deterministic rules flag the tells above, plus quality problems like cramped padding and skipped headings. No LLM, no API key.

 Impeccable is strongest on interfaces that already exist: point it at a page or a component and iterate. It builds new pages too; see Build something new for how to get the most out of that harder mode. To start, pick one component:

 /impeccable critique the pricing cards

 How it works

 Run /impeccable init once per project. It reads your code, asks only what it can't infer (who the product is for, what it needs to do, the constraints), and writes PRODUCT.md . Every later command reads it. Run /impeccable document to capture your existing visual system in DESIGN.md , so changes stay on-brand. More on context files .

 Then name a command and a target:

 /impeccable critique the onboarding flow
/impeccable quieter the landing page
/impeccable polish settings
/impeccable harden checkout

 Or just describe what you want: /impeccable redo this hero section . Narrow targets get better results; a single section reviewed closely beats a whole page at a glance. Pin a command you use often with /impeccable pin audit to get /audit as its own shortcut.

 24 commands

 Commands

 Steer
 bolder amplifies safe designs · quieter tones down loud ones · distill removes what the page doesn't need · colorize brings color to a gray interface · typeset fixes fonts, hierarchy, and sizing · layout fixes spacing and rhythm · animate adds transitions and interaction feedback · delight adds personality · overdrive goes for shaders, spring physics, and scroll-driven effects

 Review
 critique is a scored UX review · audit is a technical quality report

 Finish
 polish is the final pass before shipping · harden covers errors, i18n, overflow, and edge cases · clarify rewrites unclear copy · adapt handles screen sizes and devices · optimize fixes loading and rendering performance · onboard designs first-run flows and empty states

 Iterate live
 live lets you pick an element in the browser and cycle through variants · generate produces variants of a named element without manual picking

 Plan and set up
 shape plans UX before code · init writes PRODUCT.md · document writes DESIGN.md · extract pulls repeated patterns into your design system

 The 24th, craft , is a deprecated alias for a plain build request. Type /impeccable alone to see the list in your agent. Each command has its own page: impeccable.style/docs .

 On Codex, open /skills or type $impeccable instead of the slash command.

 Live mode

 /impeccable live opens your running dev server with an overlay. Select an element, pick a direction, and Impeccable hot-swaps variants in place. Accept one and it is written back to your source. It works with Vite, Next, SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt, and plain HTML. Iterate in the browser .

 Live mode edits a local checkout only; don't inject it into a deployed site or weaken a production CSP to make it work. Applying copy edits runs your package.json 's optional impeccable:manual-edit-validate script with your permissions, so review it before using live mode in an unfamiliar repo.

 Apply sends staged copy edits to your chat agent while a live session is polling. If none has polled in the last minute, it runs the codex CLI from your PATH instead (or claude when codex is missing), with approvals, permission checks, and sandboxing off ( --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox or --permission-mode bypassPermissions ) and your environment inherited. Its prompt carries the staged edits, the edited elements' HTML and nearby text, the page URL, and candidate source paths. Set IMPECCABLE_LIVE_COPY_AGENT=chat in the environment that starts live mode to keep Apply in your chat session, or off to disable Apply. The server reads it once at startup.

 Three ways to run the detector

 In your agent. The design hook scans every UI file your agent edits and hands the findings back before the agent calls the work done. This is where most slop gets caught: without the hook, the detector only runs when someone remembers to run it. It's available on Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, and Hermes Agent, and the installer sets it up. Say yes. Automatic design checks .

 In CI or your terminal. The CLI needs no agent:

 npx impeccable detect src/ # scan a directory
npx impeccable detect https://example.com # scan a rendered page (uses your installed Chrome or Edge)
npx impeccable detect --json . # machine-readable output
npx impeccable detect --github src/ # GitHub Actions annotations
npx impeccable detect --list-rules # every rule with its id and description

 Source files like JSX and TSX get the pattern rules only. Rules that need a rendered page, such as low contrast and tiny text, run when you scan a URL, so point the CLI at your dev server too: npx impeccable detect http://localhost:5173 .

 Exit code 2 means findings, 1 means a target couldn't be scanned. To allow your brand font everywhere, run npx impeccable ignores add-value overused-font Inter --reason "Brand font" . To turn a rule off for one file, add a comment: <!-- impeccable-disable overused-font: exported brand doc --> . Run a detector scan · Configuration and ignores .

 In your browser. The Chrome extension overlays the same findings on any live page, yours or anyone else's. Review with a visual overlay .

 Installation

 npx impeccable install

 The installer detects your coding tools, asks whether to install for this project or globally, and offers the design hook where your tool supports one. Accept the hook. Reload your tool afterward. npx impeccable update refreshes an existing install. For scripts, pass --providers=claude,codex,cursor and --scope=project|global .

 Three tools need one more step before the hook runs. In Codex, open /hooks and approve the project hook (again after an update that changes it). In Grok Build, run /hooks-trust or launch with --trust . In Hermes Agent, the hook is a plugin: run hermes plugins enable impeccable-design-hook once. Allow the hook in your harness .

 Node is only needed for npx . The skill itself runs a self-contained engine binary that ships next to it or downloads once into ~/.impeccable/bin/ .

 Claude Code, Copilot, and Grok plugins
 Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable , then open /plugin and install Impeccable.

 GitHub Copilot in VS Code: install Impeccable from the Visual Studio Marketplace or run code --install-extension renaissance-geek.impeccable . Needs VS Code 1.109.3+, Copilot Chat, and a trusted workspace. It installs the skill without the hook. Details .

 Grok Build: grok plugin install pbakaus/impeccable#plugin --trust installs the skill, agents, and hook.

 Git submodule (a pinned version for the whole team)
 git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable vendor/impeccable
npx impeccable link --source=vendor/impeccable --providers=claude,cursor

 Commit .gitmodules , the submodule, and the generated links. Teammates run git submodule update --init --recursive . To upgrade, run git submodule update --remote vendor/impeccable , rerun the link command, and commit. Linking installs skills, not hooks. Existing skill folders stay put unless you pass --force .

 Manual copy, no Node required
 Download the ZIP for your tool from impeccable.style , or clone this repo: each tool's build is committed at the repo root. Copy skills/impeccable from the folder below into the same place in your project, or into the global folder.

 Claude Code

 Cursor

 Devin
 .devin/

 GitHub Copilot

 Gemini CLI
 .gemini/

 Google Antigravity

 OpenCode
 .opencode/

 Grok Build

 Hermes Agent

 DeepSeek Harness
 .dsh/
 ${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/

 Pi

 Qoder

 Rovo Dev

 Mistral Vibe

 For example: mkdir -p your-project/.claude/skills && cp -r .claude/skills/impeccable your-project/.claude/skills/ .

 Notes:

- A manual copy skips the design hook and subagents. Run npx impeccable install to get them; it writes each tool's hook pointing at the right skill path.

- OpenCode also needs .opencode/commands/impeccable.md copied into your project's .opencode/commands/ to provide /impeccable .

- Hermes asks you to trust project-local skills once: run hermes skills trust from the project root. Global installs need no trust step.

- Cursor and Gemini CLI may need Agent Skills enabled in settings. See the Cursor and Gemini CLI skills docs.

- Restart Trae after copying.

- impeccable install and update manage a DeepSeek Harness global copy only when DSH_HOME is inside your home directory.

 Project files and git

 Impeccable writes its working files under .impeccable/ . A few are shared project artifacts and belong in the repo: config.json , live/config.json , design.json , surfaces/*.md , and critique/*.md . Keep PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md in the repo too. The rest is screenshots, caches, and runtime state.

 Copy the .gitignore entries
 # impeccable-ignore-start
 # Ephemeral output, runtime state, and per-dev overrides.
 # The **/ prefix covers .impeccable at the repo root or in a nested workspace.
 # Shared artifacts stay tracked: config.json, live/config.json,
 # design.json, surfaces/*.md, critique/*.md.
 ** / .impeccable / config.local.json
 ** / .impeccable / hook.cache.json
 ** / .impeccable / hook.pending.json
 ** / .impeccable / * .png
 ** / .impeccable / review /

 ** / .impeccable / live / server.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / sessions /

 ** / .impeccable / live / annotations /
 ** / .impeccable / live / cache /
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-apply-transaction.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-events.jsonl
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-evidence /
 ** / .impeccable / live / pending-manual-edits.json

readmeText:
video-shotcraft

 English | 中文 | 繁體中文 | 日本語 | Русский

 ▶ Browse all 150 shots in the Gallery · 🎬 Watch the Showcase

 What it does

 Tell Claude Code or Codex "make a promo for my product". The agent captures your real pages, picks shots
from a library of tuned motion recipes, storyboards the film, animates it with
 Remotion , cuts it to the beat, adds sound design, checks every frame and hands you
a finished MP4 you can keep editing.

 It is not a video generator. Every frame is drawn by code from your own screenshots and copy, so the result is
sharp, on-brand and fully editable.

 How it works

 What's new

 Important

 🎬 2026-10 · Shot library refresh

 All 216 demos were polished and reviewed. The best versions now make up
 124 cards / 150 shots , with fresh Gallery previews and video-shotcraft branding.

- 2026-09 · Motion Workbench . Keep editing the delivered film in a CapCut-style browser editor.

- 2026-08 · video-talkcraft , the narration-video
sibling: script + voiceover in, every motion beat locked to the voice
( 78 narration previews ).

- 2026-08 · JianYing (CapCut CN) export. The final film becomes an editable JianYing draft: per-shot clips,
native caption tracks, separate SFX/BGM tracks. Verified on JianYing Pro 11.2 for macOS
( guide ).

 ❤️ Sponsors

 APIMart

 Thanks to APIMart for sponsoring this project! APIMart is a low-cost API platform for AI image & video generation — GPT-Image-2 from $0.006/image, 160+ images per dollar. One async API covers both image and video: submit a task, get an ID, fetch results via polling or callback. Batch tens of thousands of images without timeouts, switch models without changing code. Pay-as-you-go with no monthly fee — sign up here to get started.

 AWS

 Amazon Web Services (AWS) offers reliable, scalable cloud computing services, including compute, storage and AI.

 Explore AWS →

 Install

 Built and tuned for Claude Code and Codex. The simplest way is to hand your agent the link:

 Install this skill for me: https://github.com/Vincentwei1021/video-shotcraft

 Or with the skills CLI:

 npx skills add Vincentwei1021/video-shotcraft

 Or by hand:

 git clone https://github.com/Vincentwei1021/video-shotcraft.git
 cd video-shotcraft
ln -s " $( pwd ) " ~ /.claude/skills/video-shotcraft # Claude Code
ln -s " $( pwd ) " ~ /.codex/skills/video-shotcraft # Codex

 In mainland China, clone from the AtomGit mirror if GitHub is slow:
 git clone https://atomgit.com/VincentWei/video-shotcraft.git .

 Use

 Just describe the film. No command needed.

 Say
 What happens

 Use video-shotcraft to make a promo for my product.
 The agent introduces the Ink Press template and asks whether to use it, then captures your pages and builds the film

 Make a launch film for this repo with the Ink Press template.
 The fastest path: your screenshots, copy and logo dropped into a validated template

 Use the deck-deal-flyin and row-embed shot cards to present this feature.
 You pick the shots by name (copy names straight from the Gallery)

 Design a product close-up inspired by spotlight-hero-card.
 One shot, adapted to your product

 Shot library

 124 recipe cards in 10 categories, 150 shots in total. Search, filter and copy card names in the
 Gallery .

 Opening & Brand · 11 shots

 text-as-mask: the product shows through the title
 Camera · 13 shots

 exploded-view: the page tilts and comes apart

 Transitions · 19 shots

 card-flock-tumble: a flock of cards becomes the headline
 Typography · 25 shots

 flying-words: a word tunnel resolves into the motto

 UI Entrance · 22 shots

 card-stack: a fan of cards deals into place
 Interaction · 13 shots

 palette-theme-ripple: a new theme ripples across the UI

 Data · 9 shots

 axis-rescale-shock: the spike breaks the axis
 Light & Emphasis · 23 shots

 spotlight-sweep: a stage light finds the title

 Rhythm · 8 shots

 paparazzi-flash: three flashes, three crops, one number
 Outro · 7 shots

 input-morph-assemble: the chat box builds the logo

 Each card lives in references/shots/<category>/<card>.md , with its Remotion implementation in
 demos/<category>/<card>/ (see demos/README.md for how to wire one into your project).

 Motion Workbench

 After delivery the skill opens a CapCut-style editor in your browser
( node workbench/scripts/open.mjs <project> ). The film is split into shot, transition, caption and SFX tracks
exactly as authored. Select any shot to edit its copy, font sizes and colours, move, trim or speed-ramp clips,
drag in any of the 150 library shots, then export with Remotion. Preview and render are frame-identical.

 Workbench guide, every panel with screenshots (Chinese) ·
 Integration contract

 Social publishing
 Optional, when you ask: publish the finished film via Upload-Post to TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn, X and more. Confirm caption and platforms, then dry-run before posting ( guide )

 Also in the box: reusable Remotion components (2.5D page camera, captions, flash cuts, digit rolls), Freesound SFX search/download tools and
5 BGM tracks, page-capture scripts, and the production method itself (capture, visual direction, storyboarding,
sound design, beat sync, final QA) in references/ .

 Showcase

 Share your film. Made something with video-shotcraft?
 Submit it with the
Showcase issue form. After review it appears on the
 Showcase page .

 Requirements

 Needs
 For

 Node.js and npm
 Remotion rendering, the template and the workbench

 ffmpeg / ffprobe
 Frame checks and final QA

 uv
 Only for BGM beat analysis (runs a one-off Python script)

 puppeteer
 Only for page capture; the capture script installs it on demand

 Remotion downloads its own headless Chrome on first render. Tested on macOS; Linux works with the notes below.

 Headless Linux / CI notes
 Rendering on a headless Linux box (tested: 2 cores, Node 22) hits three walls:

- Concurrency cap. remotion still/render fails with "Maximum for --concurrency is 2" on low-core
machines. Pass --concurrency=1 .

- Old headless removal. Recent Chrome/Chromium dropped the old headless mode, so pointing Remotion at
system Chromium fails to launch. Use a chrome-headless-shell binary instead of full Chrome.

- Blocked CDN. If remotion.media is unreachable (common in mainland China), the automatic headless-shell
download fails. Pass --browser-executable=<path-to-local chrome-headless-shell> .

 With these three flags, frame renders from the bundled template work.

 video-shotcraft/
├── SKILL.md # Agent entry point and core production rules
├── references/
│ ├── pipeline.md # End-to-end production workflow

├── demos/ # Remotion reference implementations (same categories)

 For the full workflow see SKILL.md , the production pipeline and the

 Audio and assets

 SFX come directly from Freesound , downloaded into each video's project.
The shared SFX library has been removed. The sourcing guide covers search,
CC0 / CC BY filtering, MP3 preview downloads, measurements and source/credit manifests. The Python CLI
uses the standard library; downloading and analysis require FFmpeg. No API key is needed.
 Sound design covers timing and mixing. The template retains its fixed
historical audio for playback and regression checks; new product videos source their SFX from Freesound.
BGM options remain in assets/audio/bgm/ .

 Product screenshots bundled with the template are demonstration assets. Replace them with screenshots of your
product before publishing, and check whether any product, customer or personal data needs to be anonymized.

- Freesound audio: each file under its recorded license; retain the project manifest and publish required CC BY credits.

teams, companies may need a paid license.

 Many recipes were distilled by studying the motion language of outstanding official product films, including
promos from ClickUp, Perplexity, Slack, Notion, Figma, Framer, Bear, Raycast, Pitch, Miro, Superhuman and
Loom . The cards document techniques (timing, easing, choreography) re-implemented from scratch; no footage,
artwork or brand assets from these films are included. All trademarks belong to their owners, and none of these
companies are affiliated with or endorse this project.

Thanks to its authors for sharing the approach of selecting sounds by source descriptions, duration,
download counts, rating counts and licenses. Video Shotcraft's search/download CLI is independently implemented.

 Thanks also to Remotion , which powers every demo and template here;

and animation communities whose published principles inform several cards; and Claude Code , with which this
library was built, iterated and QA'd using the same workflow the skill teaches.

representativeRepos.readmeText:
security-audit

 A coding-agent skill that turns your agent into a security auditor. It orchestrates isolated agents through reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured output, independent record verification, and target-neutral reporting.

 This is the skill that seeded Cloudflare's vulnerability discovery harness, described in Build your own vulnerability harness . The harness grew into a multi-stage, fleet-wide system; this skill is the single-repo starting point it evolved from.

 What it does

 The skill runs a structured audit in six phases:

- Reconnaissance -- map architecture, trust boundaries, input surfaces, prior evidence, and deterministic coverage in architecture.md and coverage-ledger.json .

- Coverage-led hunting -- assign isolated hunters from ledger units, record their checks, and use coverage critics to find gaps.

- Candidate validation -- give every unique candidate to a fresh verifier that tries to disprove it.

- Structured output -- write confirmed , needs_validation , and rejected records to findings.json and validate them against report-schema.json .

- Independent record verification -- fresh agents verify final source claims. Material replacements receive another independent verifier.

- Target-neutral reporting -- derive REPORT.md , FINDINGS-DETAIL.md , and NEEDS-VALIDATION.md from the verified records and coverage ledger.

 The parent runs validate-coverage-ledger.cjs after creating the ledger and after each later ledger update. It runs validate-findings.cjs in Phase 4 and again after every Phase 5 replacement.

 The verdicts are distinct: confirmed has a complete source trace and bounded observed result, needs_validation has an exact unresolved fact and no severity, and rejected records a disproved candidate.

 Multiple runs against the same repo are additive. The skill uses prior ledgers and findings to target gaps, revalidate changed source, and carry forward current-source evidence without treating stale or unresolved work as covered.

 Files

 File
 Purpose

 SKILL.md
 Setup, core principles, platform terminology, workflow overview, and audit anti-patterns

 RECONNAISSANCE.md
 Phase 1 reconnaissance prompts and synthesis instructions

 HUNTING.md
 Phase 2 orchestration, hunting methodology, and validation rules

 ATTACK-CLASSES.md
 Core, wildcard, and obvious-things attack prompts

 MEMORY-SAFETY-AND-BINARY.md
 Memory-safety, binary, and kernel hunting classes for native targets

 AI-AND-LLM.md
 Prompt-injection, agent/tool, and output-handling hunting classes for LLM-backed targets

 WEB-PROTOCOL-AND-AUTH.md
 HTTP request-framing, cache, and authentication-protocol hunting classes for HTTP-protocol and auth targets

 CLIENT-SIDE.md
 DOM-injection, messaging-trust, UI-redress, and prototype-pollution hunting classes for client-side/browser targets

 SUPPLY-CHAIN-AND-RELEASE.md
 Dependency, CI, release, signing, update, plugin, and extension hunting classes

 CLOUD-AND-DEPLOYMENT.md
 IAM, infrastructure-as-code, container, serverless, ingress, and runtime-configuration hunting classes

 PROTOCOLS-RPC-AND-MESSAGING.md
 RPC, serialization, queue, broker, webhook, and streaming-protocol hunting classes

 RESOURCE-EXHAUSTION-AND-AVAILABILITY.md
 Shared resource, quota, queue, worker, and operator-spend hunting classes

 DATA-ISOLATION-AND-LIFECYCLE.md
 Tenant isolation, cache, search, export, backup, migration, deletion, and restore hunting classes

 DESKTOP-MOBILE-AND-LOCAL-IPC.md
 Native app, deep-link, webview, exported-component, helper, daemon, and local-IPC hunting classes

 VALIDATION-AND-REPORTING.md
 Phases 3–6 candidate validation, structured output, record verification, and reporting

 report-schema.json
 JSON schema for all three findings.json verdicts

 validate-findings.cjs
 Zero-dependency validator for findings.json in Phases 4 and 5

 validate-findings.test.cjs
 Findings-validator tests and producer-compatible fixture checks

 validate-coverage-ledger.cjs
 Zero-dependency validator for coverage-ledger.json in Phases 1–5

 validate-coverage-ledger.test.cjs
 Coverage-ledger validator tests

 Installation

 Install the skill with the Skills CLI :

 npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill \
 --skill security-audit

 Use --global for a user-level installation:

 npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill \
 --skill security-audit \
 --global

 Run npx skills --help for agent-selection and non-interactive options.

 Usage

 Start your coding agent in (or pointed at) the codebase you want to audit, then ask it to do a security audit:

 security audit this codebase

 find security vulnerabilities in ./src

 do a security review, output to ~/audits/my-project

 The skill activates automatically when the request matches its trigger (security audit, find vulnerabilities, pen-test the code, etc.). A direct codebase audit or pen-test request uses full audit mode. Security questions and focused vulnerability work use guidance mode unless you request report artifacts. In full audit mode, an unspecified output directory defaults to ~/security-audit-skill/<repo-name>/run-<N> . The workflow writes inside the target repository only when you explicitly select a directory that version control ignores.

 Requirements

- A coding agent with a model that supports tool use and parallel sub-agents

- Node.js for the zero-dependency findings and coverage-ledger validators

- An OS-enforced sandbox for target-controlled builds, tests, processes, browsers, emulators, fuzzers, and fixtures. It must disable external networking, use a sanitized allowlisted environment, enforce resource limits, and allow writes only to assigned scratch paths. Without these controls, the workflow keeps the lead as needs_validation instead of executing target code.

 Design principles

- Only confirm established boundary failures. Keep a source-grounded blocked lead as needs_validation with its exact unresolved fact.

- Adversarial validation. The agent that checks a finding is never the agent that found it.

- Severity requires impact. Likelihood x impact, not deviation from a checklist.

- Defense-in-depth gaps are not vulnerabilities. If Layer A prevents the attack, the absence of Layer B is a hardening note.

- Multiple runs improve coverage. In our test runs, a single run found roughly half of the vulnerabilities that repeated runs found in total.

 Contact

 Questions, feedback, or comparing notes on AI-driven security tooling: security-ai-research@cloudflare.com

 License

 MIT -- see LICENSE .

representativeRepos.readmeText:
T3 Code

 The open-source control plane for coding agents.

 Download ·
 iOS ·
 Android ·
 Web ·
 Docs ·
 Discord

 T3 Code runs the coding agents on your machine and gives them one fast interface. Start a thread at your desk, then approve the next step from your phone.

 It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok Build, Antigravity, Kiro, Pi, Muse Code, fx, and any ACP agent. If an agent is set up on your computer, T3 Code can control it.

 What you get

- Your subscriptions. T3 Code does not resell tokens. It drives the agents you are already signed in to.

- Every agent in one place. Change models in the middle of a thread. Let Claude hand a task to Codex.

- Desktop, web, and phone. One server, and every client shows the same threads. There are apps for iOS and Android.

- Remote ready. Run agents on any machine. Connect over your local network, Tailscale, or T3 Connect .

- Git built in. Each thread can work in its own worktree. Review the diff, then commit, push, and open a pull request with one button.

- Fast. Performance is a feature here. We measure it, and we treat a dropped frame as a bug.

- Open. MIT licensed. If you don't like something, fork it.

 Install

 Desktop app

 Download T3 Code for macOS, Windows, or Linux. You can also use a package manager:

 Platform
 Command

 macOS
 brew install --cask t3-code

 Windows
 winget install T3Tools.T3Code or scoop install extras/t3code

 Arch Linux
 yay -S t3code-bin

 Nix
 nix profile add github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable#t3code

 Debian, Ubuntu
 .deb from Releases

 Command line

 This installs the t3 command. Run t3 to start the server and open the web app.

 curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh

 On Windows, in PowerShell:

 irm https: // t3.codes / install.ps1 | iex

 To try it once without an install, run npx t3@latest .

 Phone

 Get the app from the App Store or Google Play . Then follow remote access to connect it to your computer.

 Sign in to an agent

 T3 Code needs one agent that is installed and signed in. For example, install Claude Code and run claude auth login , or install Codex CLI and run codex login .

 Provider setup has the steps for each agent. Install T3 Code covers nightly builds, AppImage, WSL, and NixOS.

 "Wait, what are you selling me?"

 Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents. We were inspired by existing solutions like the Codex desktop app, Conductor, Claude Desktop and Cursor Glass, but none met our bar.

 We wanted something performant, remote-ready, and truly open. If we ever go the wrong direction, we want you to have everything you need to fork and build the tool that you want.

 Documentation

- Install and first run

- Remote access from a phone or another machine

- Permission modes

- Source control

- Connect outside agents over MCP

- FAQ

 All docs has the full list.

 Contributing

 We have limited review capacity. Small, focused fixes are the most likely to be merged. Features need an approved discussion first.

- Read CONTRIBUTING.md before you report a bug or open a pull request.

- Put feature requests in Ideas .

- Build from source with the development runbook . The architecture overview explains how it works.

- Get help in Discord .

 License

 MIT

representativeRepos.readmeText:
Impeccable

 The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with polish and bolder , review with critique and audit , and catch AI slop before it ships.

 From your project root:

 npx impeccable install

 Reload your coding tool, then run /impeccable init in your agent ( $impeccable init on Codex).

 Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Replit Agent, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and Veto. Full docs live at impeccable.style/docs .

 Without Impeccable
 With Impeccable

 Same model (Fable 5.1), same brief: a fourteen-room family guesthouse on the Ligurian coast. Without Impeccable, it builds the tasteful default: cream page, thin serif, italic accent, pill buttons. With it, the page is built around one picture: the house at night, seen from the water.

 For a full project, see the Neo Mirai case study : a conference site taken from mockup to shipped page.

 Why

 Inter for everything. Purple-to-blue gradients. Cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, a rounded-square icon tile above every heading. Ask an agent for a page with no other guidance and these show up again and again, across models and projects.

- Words for what you want. "Make it pop" leaves your agent to guess. /impeccable bolder the pricing cards loads a playbook written for that one move and points it at one target.

- A reviewer. critique scores the design against usability heuristics and ranks what to fix first. audit checks accessibility, performance, theming, and responsive behavior, with findings ranked P0 (blocking) to P3 (polish).

- A slop detector. 62 deterministic rules flag the tells above, plus quality problems like cramped padding and skipped headings. No LLM, no API key.

 Impeccable is strongest on interfaces that already exist: point it at a page or a component and iterate. It builds new pages too; see Build something new for how to get the most out of that harder mode. To start, pick one component:

 /impeccable critique the pricing cards

 How it works

 Run /impeccable init once per project. It reads your code, asks only what it can't infer (who the product is for, what it needs to do, the constraints), and writes PRODUCT.md . Every later command reads it. Run /impeccable document to capture your existing visual system in DESIGN.md , so changes stay on-brand. More on context files .

 Then name a command and a target:

 /impeccable critique the onboarding flow
/impeccable quieter the landing page
/impeccable polish settings
/impeccable harden checkout

 Or just describe what you want: /impeccable redo this hero section . Narrow targets get better results; a single section reviewed closely beats a whole page at a glance. Pin a command you use often with /impeccable pin audit to get /audit as its own shortcut.

 24 commands

 Commands

 Steer
 bolder amplifies safe designs · quieter tones down loud ones · distill removes what the page doesn't need · colorize brings color to a gray interface · typeset fixes fonts, hierarchy, and sizing · layout fixes spacing and rhythm · animate adds transitions and interaction feedback · delight adds personality · overdrive goes for shaders, spring physics, and scroll-driven effects

 Review
 critique is a scored UX review · audit is a technical quality report

 Finish
 polish is the final pass before shipping · harden covers errors, i18n, overflow, and edge cases · clarify rewrites unclear copy · adapt handles screen sizes and devices · optimize fixes loading and rendering performance · onboard designs first-run flows and empty states

 Iterate live
 live lets you pick an element in the browser and cycle through variants · generate produces variants of a named element without manual picking

 Plan and set up
 shape plans UX before code · init writes PRODUCT.md · document writes DESIGN.md · extract pulls repeated patterns into your design system

 The 24th, craft , is a deprecated alias for a plain build request. Type /impeccable alone to see the list in your agent. Each command has its own page: impeccable.style/docs .

 On Codex, open /skills or type $impeccable instead of the slash command.

 Live mode

 /impeccable live opens your running dev server with an overlay. Select an element, pick a direction, and Impeccable hot-swaps variants in place. Accept one and it is written back to your source. It works with Vite, Next, SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt, and plain HTML. Iterate in the browser .

 Live mode edits a local checkout only; don't inject it into a deployed site or weaken a production CSP to make it work. Applying copy edits runs your package.json 's optional impeccable:manual-edit-validate script with your permissions, so review it before using live mode in an unfamiliar repo.

 Apply sends staged copy edits to your chat agent while a live session is polling. If none has polled in the last minute, it runs the codex CLI from your PATH instead (or claude when codex is missing), with approvals, permission checks, and sandboxing off ( --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox or --permission-mode bypassPermissions ) and your environment inherited. Its prompt carries the staged edits, the edited elements' HTML and nearby text, the page URL, and candidate source paths. Set IMPECCABLE_LIVE_COPY_AGENT=chat in the environment that starts live mode to keep Apply in your chat session, or off to disable Apply. The server reads it once at startup.

 Three ways to run the detector

 In your agent. The design hook scans every UI file your agent edits and hands the findings back before the agent calls the work done. This is where most slop gets caught: without the hook, the detector only runs when someone remembers to run it. It's available on Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, and Hermes Agent, and the installer sets it up. Say yes. Automatic design checks .

 In CI or your terminal. The CLI needs no agent:

 npx impeccable detect src/ # scan a directory
npx impeccable detect https://example.com # scan a rendered page (uses your installed Chrome or Edge)
npx impeccable detect --json . # machine-readable output
npx impeccable detect --github src/ # GitHub Actions annotations
npx impeccable detect --list-rules # every rule with its id and description

 Source files like JSX and TSX get the pattern rules only. Rules that need a rendered page, such as low contrast and tiny text, run when you scan a URL, so point the CLI at your dev server too: npx impeccable detect http://localhost:5173 .

 Exit code 2 means findings, 1 means a target couldn't be scanned. To allow your brand font everywhere, run npx impeccable ignores add-value overused-font Inter --reason "Brand font" . To turn a rule off for one file, add a comment: <!-- impeccable-disable overused-font: exported brand doc --> . Run a detector scan · Configuration and ignores .

 In your browser. The Chrome extension overlays the same findings on any live page, yours or anyone else's. Review with a visual overlay .

 Installation

 npx impeccable install

 The installer detects your coding tools, asks whether to install for this project or globally, and offers the design hook where your tool supports one. Accept the hook. Reload your tool afterward. npx impeccable update refreshes an existing install. For scripts, pass --providers=claude,codex,cursor and --scope=project|global .

 Three tools need one more step before the hook runs. In Codex, open /hooks and approve the project hook (again after an update that changes it). In Grok Build, run /hooks-trust or launch with --trust . In Hermes Agent, the hook is a plugin: run hermes plugins enable impeccable-design-hook once. Allow the hook in your harness .

 Node is only needed for npx . The skill itself runs a self-contained engine binary that ships next to it or downloads once into ~/.impeccable/bin/ .

 Claude Code, Copilot, and Grok plugins
 Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable , then open /plugin and install Impeccable.

 GitHub Copilot in VS Code: install Impeccable from the Visual Studio Marketplace or run code --install-extension renaissance-geek.impeccable . Needs VS Code 1.109.3+, Copilot Chat, and a trusted workspace. It installs the skill without the hook. Details .

 Grok Build: grok plugin install pbakaus/impeccable#plugin --trust installs the skill, agents, and hook.

 Git submodule (a pinned version for the whole team)
 git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable vendor/impeccable
npx impeccable link --source=vendor/impeccable --providers=claude,cursor

 Commit .gitmodules , the submodule, and the generated links. Teammates run git submodule update --init --recursive . To upgrade, run git submodule update --remote vendor/impeccable , rerun the link command, and commit. Linking installs skills, not hooks. Existing skill folders stay put unless you pass --force .

 Manual copy, no Node required
 Download the ZIP for your tool from impeccable.style , or clone this repo: each tool's build is committed at the repo root. Copy skills/impeccable from the folder below into the same place in your project, or into the global folder.

 Tool

 Claude Code

 Cursor

 Codex CLI, Replit Agent
 .agents/
 ~/.agents/skills/

 Devin
 .devin/

 GitHub Copilot

 Gemini CLI
 .gemini/

 Google Antigravity
 .agent/

 OpenCode
 .opencode/

 Grok Build

 Hermes Agent
 .hermes/
 ${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/

 DeepSeek Harness
 .dsh/
 ${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/

 Pi
 .pi/

 Qoder

 ~/.qoder/skills/

 Rovo Dev
 .rovodev/

 Mistral Vibe
 .vibe/

 Trae China
 .trae-cn/
 ~/.trae-cn/skills/

 For example: mkdir -p your-project/.claude/skills && cp -r .claude/skills/impeccable your-project/.claude/skills/ .

 Notes:

- A manual copy skips the design hook and subagents. Run npx impeccable install to get them; it writes each tool's hook pointing at the right skill path.

- OpenCode also needs .opencode/commands/impeccable.md copied into your project's .opencode/commands/ to provide /impeccable .

- Hermes asks you to trust project-local skills once: run hermes skills trust from the project root. Global installs need no trust step.

- Cursor and Gemini CLI may need Agent Skills enabled in settings. See the Cursor and Gemini CLI skills docs.

- Restart Trae after copying.

- impeccable install and update manage a DeepSeek Harness global copy only when DSH_HOME is inside your home directory.

 Project files and git

 Impeccable writes its working files under .impeccable/ . A few are shared project artifacts and belong in the repo: config.json , live/config.json , design.json , surfaces/*.md , and critique/*.md . Keep PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md in the repo too. The rest is screenshots, caches, and runtime state.

 Copy the .gitignore entries
 # impeccable-ignore-start
 # Ephemeral output, runtime state, and per-dev overrides.
 # The **/ prefix covers .impeccable at the repo root or in a nested workspace.
 # Shared artifacts stay tracked: config.json, live/config.json,
 # design.json, surfaces/*.md, critique/*.md.
 ** / .impeccable / config.local.json
 ** / .impeccable / hook.cache.json
 ** / .impeccable / hook.pending.json
 ** / .impeccable / * .png
 ** / .impeccable / review /
 ** / .impeccable / questions /
 ** / .impeccable / live / server.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / sessions /
 ** / .impeccable / live / previews /
 ** / .impeccable / live / annotations /
 ** / .impeccable / live / cache /
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-apply-transaction.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-events.jsonl
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-evidence /
 ** / .impeccable / live / pending-manual-edits.json
 ** / .impeccab...

readmeText:
agent-browser

 Browser automation for AI agents: open pages, read them as an accessibility tree, and act on elements from the shell.

 agent-browser is a native Rust CLI that gives an AI agent a browser it can drive one command at a time. snapshot returns the page as compact text with a ref such as @e1 for each element. The agent acts on a ref, reads the page again to check the result, and repeats. The browser stays open between commands, so each step is one short shell call.

 Install

 npm install -g agent-browser
agent-browser install # download Chrome for Testing (first time only)

- Homebrew: brew install agent-browser , then agent-browser install .

- Linux: agent-browser install --with-deps also installs the browser's system libraries.

- No install: npx agent-browser open example.com .

 Project installs, building from source, upgrade , and doctor are covered in Installation .

 Quick start

 agent-browser open example.com
agent-browser snapshot -i # interactive elements, each with a ref
agent-browser click @e1 # act on a ref from that snapshot
agent-browser get url # check the result
agent-browser close

 The snapshot for example.com :

 - link "Learn more" [ref=e1]

- Refs describe the page at the time of the snapshot. After navigation or a DOM change, take a new snapshot before using refs again.

- CSS selectors, text, XPath, and semantic locators also work, for example agent-browser find role button click --name "Submit" . See Selectors .

- A click fails, instead of reporting success, when the target is hidden, disabled, outside the viewport, or covered by another element such as a consent banner. Dismiss the covering element, take a new snapshot, and retry.

 The full walkthrough is in the quick start .

 How it works

 The CLI sends each command to a background daemon that starts on the first command and controls the browser over the Chrome DevTools Protocol. Each --session gets its own daemon and browser. By default, the daemon closes a headless browser and exits after one hour without commands, saving state first when session persistence is configured.

 Chrome for Testing is the default browser. You can also attach to a running Chrome with --cdp or --auto-connect ( CDP mode ), select the Lightpanda or Obscura engine with --engine , drive Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator , or use a cloud browser provider such as Browserbase , Browserless , Browser Use , Kernel , or AgentCore .

 For AI agents

 The CLI ships skills that match its version:

 agent-browser skills get core # the core loop, refs, waiting, and common workflows
agent-browser skills get core --ref commands # one reference, such as the full command list
agent-browser skills get core --full # adds the full command reference and templates
agent-browser skills list # specialized skills: electron, slack, dogfood, and more

 Install the discovery skill into an agent harness from skills.sh :

 npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-browser

 The installed skill is a thin stub that tells the agent to load agent-browser skills get core , so its instructions always match the installed CLI. Or add this to your AGENTS.md :

 Use ` agent-browser ` for browser automation. Before the first use, run
 ` agent-browser skills get core ` and follow it.

 For MCP clients, agent-browser mcp starts an MCP server over stdio. See MCP server .

 Commands

 Run agent-browser --help for the full list, or agent-browser <command> --help for one command.

 Group
 Commands
 Docs

 Navigate and read
 open , back , forward , reload , read , snapshot , get , is
 Core , Snapshots

 Interact
 click , dblclick , fill , type , press , keyboard , hover , focus , select , check , uncheck , scroll , drag , upload , mouse , find
 Core , Find elements

 Wait
 wait
 Wait

 Capture
 screenshot , pdf , record , download , diff
 Recording , Diffing , Files

 Page and network state
 cookies , storage , network , set , clipboard , eval , pushstate
 Network , Settings

 Tabs, frames, and dialogs
 tab , frame , dialog
 Tabs and frames

 Debug and performance
 console , errors , highlight , inspect , trace , profiler , vitals , react , a11y
 Debugging , Profiler , React

 Sessions and auth
 session , state , auth , profiles , confirm , deny
 Sessions , Security

 Agents and integrations
 skills , mcp , webmcp , flow , chat , batch , plugin
 Skills , WebMCP , Plugins

 Observe
 stream , dashboard
 Streaming , Dashboard

 Setup
 install , upgrade , doctor , connect , close
 Installation

 Flags, environment variables, and agent-browser.json are documented in Configuration .

 Platforms

 Native binaries ship for macOS (ARM64, x64), Linux (ARM64, x64, glibc and musl), and Windows (x64). The npm package picks the right binary for the host.

 Development

 Building from source requires Node.js 24 or later, pnpm 11 or later, and Rust:

 pnpm install
pnpm build:source # builds the dashboard and the native CLI
pnpm link --global
agent-browser install

 Run the Rust checks from cli/ :

 cargo fmt -- --check
cargo clippy
cargo test
cargo test e2e -- --ignored --test-threads=1 # launches real headless Chrome

 AGENTS.md lists the files to update with each change, the docs checks, and the release process.

 Documentation

- agent-browser.dev : introduction, guides, and reference

- Commands and Configuration

- Security : the auth vault, domain allowlists, action policies, and content boundaries

- Next.js and Vercel and eve : running agent-browser in Vercel Sandbox and eve agents

- Changelog

rule.overview: 本期高增项目的最大公约数不是单个插件或脚本，而是让 AI 真正接入真实仓库、真实上下文和真实研发流程的工程化能力。
rule.what: 高 Star 增量项目正在从“补一个能力点”演进为“补一整条研发链路”，共同指向 AI 编程增强与工程化工作流这一集群化方向。
rule.why: 社区集体发力的根因，是大模型在大型代码库中存在上下文窗口受限、仓库级记忆缺失和任务交接脆弱等瓶颈，迫使 AI 编程从单文件补全转向全库架构级理解与执行。
rule.how: 支撑这一趋势落地的底层支撑，正在收敛为 MCP 接口、仓库级索引/RAG、代码知识图谱、终端工作流接入以及可编排的 Agent 链路。
rule.risk: 潜在风险在于，很多项目仍停留在工作流包装层，若缺少稳定的上下文管理、索引质量和可验证执行闭环，工程化承诺容易沦为演示效果。
